title: 2026-08-09-interpretation-correctness-posture
body: Interpretation-correctness real-model leg — under deterministic L4 (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`) a canned `L4Output` replaces the inference, so every live leg exercises the plumbing and never the interpretation: "Conductor green" does not mean Pulse's interpretation is trustworthy. Prove the real thing — deterministic mode OFF, a known root cause injected, the top hypothesis asserted to identify it (the P-033 path Pulse's own memo calls the single most important test in all of Pulse). Needs real per-check read-back extraction (v2-09) AND a non-deterministic live leg that can never be a CI gate, which is why it is not an 0.2.0 entry. Covers the diagnostic-quality cluster P-031/P-033/P-034/P-044, pinned meanwhile in `conductor_core::UNBACKED_AUTO` and asserted by `check_scenario_backing`.

title: 2026-08-31-p-075-assert-round
body: `incident_events`-through-MCP — Pulse's corpus persists incident lifecycle events (created/resolved) in `incident_events`, the ONE corpus table whose content is not L4-authored and therefore the only remaining candidate for payload-level read-back fidelity under deterministic L4. Measured 2026-09-01 at Pulse HEAD `83d4060`: ZERO references in `crates/mcp-server` — written by `crates/triage/src/incident/persistence.rs::save_incident_event`, read only corpus-side (`crates/corpus/src/disposition.rs` + a `contract.rs` test helper) — so no MCP tool surfaces it at any width and Conductor cannot reach it. This is a PULSE-side capability gap, not Conductor work: surfacing it needs a new or extended MCP tool on the SUT, which the operator routed to Pulse's 0.4.0 incubator where it pairs with the big-brother MCP direction. Until then payload fidelity stays unattainable and Conductor asserts runtime-STATE fidelity instead (`mark_incident_resolved` + active-set membership, live-proven that chunk).

title: 2026-09-09-workspace-formatting-pass-and-a-fmt-ci-gate
body: `v2-24` routine a11y specs — deferred in 0.2.0 because the runtime-major hypothesis was FALSIFIED, not because the work was descoped: CI run 34280136892 installed Evergreen 152.0.4191.66 and `DevToolsActivePort` still never appeared within 90s with the app alive and three webview children resident, so the hosted `windows-2025` image opens no remote-debugging endpoint **[premise-corrected 2026-09-17 — CONFIGURATION-BOUND, not unconditional: the endpoint does NOT open on hosted `windows-2025` at runtime 152/153, and DOES open on hosted `windows-2022` at a coherent 131.0.2903.86 driver/runtime pair at High integrity. run 35192876641: hosted `windows-2022` at a COHERENT 131.0.2903.86 msedgedriver+WebView2-runtime pair, High integrity — `DevToolsActivePort` in 1 s, WebDriver session created (`status 200`, banner `[webview2 131.0.2903.86 windows]`), routine arm 11 passing / 1 failing / 2 skipped; the single red `:384` is a counting-basis defect in the assertion (12 visits / 6 distinct), not an a11y defect. Corroborated externally by actions/runner-images#14738, which reports the same split on a byte-identical image (`windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587) and runtime (152.0.4191.66) for a plain Tauri/wry app with no token or integrity work. Integrity's SIGN is configuration-bound, so the 2026-09-16 dev-host legs A/B/C are BOUNDED by this, never retired.]** under EITHER runtime major. Re-open on three unmeasured candidates, cheapest first: a hosted-image policy on remote debugging (an Edge/WebView2 policy registry read is the one-line probe) · a session or service-account property of the runner · msedgedriver 151 against a 152 runtime as a cause of the DRIVER failing to start, an axis never tested (skew was retired only as a cause of the ENDPOINT failing to open). Also carry the upstream finding, RE-SCOPED 2026-09-11: the routine arm's red is INTERMITTENT between two failure modes, so `v3-02` re-measures rather than inherits either framing. A tauri-driver bind refusal was observed in runs 34162118841 / 34251573399 / 34256490781 at runtime 151 (four refused POSTs inside ~1.5 s against a 6.9 s driver bind — a startup race predating both the upgrade and any skew), but it did NOT reproduce at run 34586959536: that run's captured log holds ZERO `ECONNREFUSED`, wdio connected to the driver and reached session creation, and the red is the ENDPOINT — `session not created: DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist`, twice (through tauri-driver and again through the driver-alone probe that bypasses it). The bind race is real on the runs it was seen on and is not the standing cause; measured at `2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed`. Self-hosted runners on a public repo are not an option.

title: 2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round
body: `constellation-severity-live-wiring` grades on TWO structurally-dead assertions — one owned item, both measured live this chunk, neither blocking the release. (1) Its `[[expected]]` `CountAtLeast >= 1` reads `evidence_count`, summed from `retrieve_telemetry_slice.span_refs`, which Pulse writes EMPTY at every production incident (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs:871` sets `EvidenceRefs.span_ids: Vec::new()`; whole-repo enumeration finds no other non-test writer; `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs:430-439` maps `span_refs` 1:1 from it) — so `0 >= 1` is false in every world and the floor routes to `CalibrationRegion` regardless of the declared `Hard` (`conductor-verify/src/slo.rs:97-100`). The mechanism was already recorded at `architecture-amendments.md:403` (2026-08-21) as the ground on which FIVE severity-lifecycle scenarios retired their checks to declare-only; this scenario is an unswept member of that ruled class, and two siblings remain — `findings-counter-refresh.toml:49` (floor 3, its unmet-floor outcome already recorded accepted at `architecture.md:69`) and `pulse-run-contract.toml:58` (floor 1). Derivation, so the next reader does not land on seven: `grep -n 'kind = "CountAtLeast"' scenarios/*.toml` → exactly 3 live keys; a bare token grep hits 7 files because 4 mention it only in retirement comments. (2) Its declared `slo_tier = "<20s"` is UNATTAINABLE by construction — `latency_ms` is `read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at`, which spans the whole emission window, and this scenario's own phases sum to 30 s (`gap_ms` 3000+15000+12000 at `:29`/`:36`/`:44`); measured `latency_ms 30212` against `deadline_ms 20000`. Recorded, not established: defect (2) plausibly ORIGINATES in the obs-plan gloss this same wrap retired — a tier chosen believing the delta ≈ an MCP round-trip would be far too tight for a 30 s window. Disposition for the next version's route Phase A: take the three-scenario `CountAtLeast` class together rather than retiring this one alone, which would contradict an accepted sibling. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-live-pulse-in-lane-scenario-round/evidence/live-round-verdict.md`. **Extended at `2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle`** (operator direction at that wrap: extend this item to the full class, take the class together, no fix in this chunk). (3) A THIRD dead assertion of the same class and a different KIND: `cross-incident-recurrence` (P-036) declares `[[expected]]` `kind = "Contains"` / `class = "Hard"` / `expected = "Previously seen"` (`scenarios/cross-incident-recurrence.toml:42-45`), and it measured DEAD on its first-ever live drive as leg 3 of this chunk's SLO pass — the read-back succeeded and the run reached a verdict, but no producer anywhere emits that token; the scenario's own header records it as INFERRED (`:15`, "the spec uses prose"), an Epoch-8/10 calibration point that was never closed. The leg was SWAPPED to `investigate-actions-functional` on operator direction and the FAIL retained as committed evidence, so the release stands on three clean legs and this stays a routed finding, not a fix this chunk owes. Evidence: `conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-09-10-release-build-and-bundle/evidence/slo-verification-pass.md` + `evidence/leg3-2026-09-10T19-40-47-134.jsonl`. (4) Retiring that declaration is NOT a TOML-only edit: `crates/conductor-core/src/scenario.rs:1188` holds `cross_incident_recurrence_asserts_previously_seen_via_hard_contains`, a `#[test]` that reads the committed TOML and asserts exactly the `Contains` / `Hard` / `"Previously seen"` triple — it goes red the moment the declaration is retired, so the fix is a PAIRED edit and the scenario file alone is a false modify-set. (5) That test is invisible to the sweep the test rules prescribe for exactly this purpose, because it lives in an INLINE `#[cfg(test)]` module under `src/` while `.claude/rules/testing.md:54` prescribes `grep -rln "<scenario-name>" crates/**/tests`. Measured at this wrap: the prescribed form exits 1 with no output, while `grep -rln "cross-incident-recurrence" crates/` returns the file. hypothesis: that blind spot is also why this declaration was left standing when the surrounding family retired its checks — plausible, not measured. The rule entry was corrected in place at this wrap, so a later reader gets the wider sweep. (6) Corpus context, re-derived at this wrap and independently by the operator (36 scenarios parsed, summed `gap_ms` per scenario against the tier thresholds 5000 / 20000 / 90000 ms): **17 of 36 declare an `slo_tier` smaller than their own summed phase duration**, and they are THREE different situations that must not be collapsed into one defect — **9** declare the ceiling `<90s` and exceed it (the ratified posture per `matrix#v2-12`, not a defect); **2** are beyond EVERY tier while declaring a smaller one (`ack-cooldown` 370 000 ms at `<20s`, `severity-tier-autonomous` 120 000 ms at `<5s`); and **6** declare a tier that a larger EXISTING tier would hold — `constellation-severity-live-wiring` (30 000 ms at `<20s`) among them, which IS defect (2) of this item. So the tier half of this residual is one member of a 6-scenario class, and retiring it alone would leave five siblings inconsistent, exactly as retiring the `CountAtLeast` alone would.

title: an external audit/dev CLI tool (e.g. cargo-audit / cargo-deny) is installed a patch/minor behind the version the securit
body:
- pattern: an external audit/dev CLI tool (e.g. cargo-audit / cargo-deny) is installed a patch/minor behind the version the security-plan names, and the gate runs green
  verdict: routine
  note: dev CLI tools can't be pinned in `Cargo.lock`; the security-plan versions are minimum FLOORS and the real signal (the RustSec advisory DB) is fetched fresh at runtime, so a tool ≥ floor running green satisfies the gate. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-15 (dependency-audit-gate wrap); security-plan §Dependency Security now states floors.

title: a Foundation-epoch chunk defers a cross-cutting concern (redaction, CI gate, coverage tooling) that the obs/security/tes
body:
- pattern: a Foundation-epoch chunk defers a cross-cutting concern (redaction, CI gate, coverage tooling) that the obs/security/test plan already sequences as a SEPARATE downstream bootstrap phase, and the deferral introduces no actual leak/violation in the current chunk
  verdict: routine
  note: a plan that lists the concern as its own bootstrap phase (e.g. obs-plan §3 `pii-scrubbing-wire`) has already sequenced it later; deferring it is build-sequencing, not drift, when the current chunk leaks nothing. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-15 (structured-logging-stack wrap; D-obs-redaction fired because logging landed before the redaction layer — which is the next chunk). Generalizes the test-runner sequencing rule above.

title: a redaction/scrubbing amendment reconciles a spec's redaction WORDING to a sound host-file-path-anchored implementation
body:
- pattern: a redaction/scrubbing amendment reconciles a spec's redaction WORDING to a sound host-file-path-anchored implementation (value-scrub on absolute host paths + field-name allowlist + Display-not-Debug edge), where the chunk report shows no actual host-path / struct-name leak
  verdict: routine
  note: when the redaction is implemented and the report demonstrates the invariant holds (host paths masked, no Debug struct dumps, allowlisted identity fields like `target` preserved), reconciling over-literal spec wording (e.g. "remove all `module::` tokens") to the sound model is documentation alignment, not a hygiene gap. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-15 (log-error-boundary-redaction wrap; D-obs-redaction escalate → reconcile §6/§11). Distinct from the deferral rule above (that was redaction NOT YET built; this is redaction built + reconciling wording).

  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-29 (by the seed rule Accurate this-chunk addition) — generalizes the redaction-reconciliation rule above to ANY spec-illustration → sound-impl alignment. title: a drift detector proposes a dependency bump / version change for a dependency the chunk's report shows it did NOT add or
body:
- pattern: a drift detector proposes a dependency bump / version change for a dependency the chunk's report shows it did NOT add or modify, where the manifest already satisfies the spec's stated floor
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — NOT this chunk's drift. The report is the single source of what changed this chunk; a dependency it never touched (already at/above the spec floor) is out of scope this wrap. The detector likely read the spec's historical rationale (e.g. "arch originally pinned tauri 2.10.1 → bump to ≥2.10.3") as a current gap. Verify against the manifest before escalating. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-16 (seeded-phase-scheduler wrap; D-security-deps escalate misfired on `tauri` — already pinned 2.10.3, untouched — while the chunk only added audit-green rand_chacha/rand_core).

title: a drift detector flags an OTel SDK crate (`opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry_sdk`) present in the dependency tree as a TRA
body:
- pattern: a drift detector flags an OTel SDK crate (`opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry_sdk`) present in the dependency tree as a TRANSITIVE dep of `opentelemetry-proto` (the PRODUCT OTLP proto lib), where the chunk report shows it is never initialized/used and self-observation remains tracing-JSON-only
  verdict: routine
  note: the no-OTel-SDK invariant (obs-plan §3/§11) is BEHAVIORAL — the harm is initializing/using an SDK for self-obs (batch tasks break `current_thread` determinism + pollute the PRODUCT stream). A dormant transitive SDK crate pulled by opentelemetry-proto's default features does not violate it (nothing runs); a `default-features = false` trim is a tracked optimization, not drift. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-17 (raw-otlp-message-scaffold wrap; D-obs-stack escalate → accept+document; obs-plan §3 now states the invariant is about SDK init/use, not tree presence).

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering a public library API symbol (struct / enum / fn / const / method) in ANY arch regi
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering a public library API symbol (struct / enum / fn / const / method) in ANY arch registry section (§Occupied Resources OR §Standard Contracts), where the chunk's actual occupied resources (ports / sockets / endpoints / IPC methods / events / env vars / workspace crates) are already registered there
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach. arch §Occupied Resources tracks OCCUPIED RESOURCES (ports/sockets/routes/crates/artifacts/env vars) and §Standard Contracts tracks the readiness-gate + run-report-envelope SHAPES — neither tracks per-crate public API surface; the detector's own enumerated list does not include library symbols. When the chunk's real resources are already registered (the `:4317` socket + the workspace crates in §Occupied Resources; the run-report envelope `verdict ∈ {Pass,Fail,CalibrationRegion}` + `slo_tier`/`latency_ms` in §Standard Contracts), registering its API symbols is detail arch deliberately omits. Precedent: the 8 conductor-emit chunks added many public symbols (RateCurve / EmitError / TraceEmitter / LatencyProfile / PiiCorpus / ServiceTopology …) and registered none — D-arch-resources returned clean on those wraps. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-19 (port-occupier-fault wrap, §Occupied Resources variant); broadened to §Standard Contracts on 2026-06-21 (expected-outcome-slo-timing-model wrap — the detector re-fired proposing ExpectedCheck/SloOutcome/CheckOutcome/evaluate_* into §Standard Contracts; same over-reach, dismissed with the user).

title: a seam PRIMITIVE (a type/constructor/fn in `conductor-core` [`resolve_hold` / `hold.*`] OR `conductor-report` [`db.inser
body:
- pattern: a seam PRIMITIVE (a type/constructor/fn in `conductor-core` [`resolve_hold` / `hold.*`] OR `conductor-report` [`db.insert_run` / `report.generate`]) route-sequences its obs span to the later timeline-wiring epoch (Epoch 7/8), and the current chunk emits no span and leaks nothing — D-obs-instrumentation fires on the primitive's arrival
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — the must-trace OPERATION is the live application under the timeline (the fault APPLICATION, or the hold AWAIT under a run), not the primitive's definition; a primitive that ships before its driver carries no must-trace op yet, so the deferred `hold.wait_resolve` / `db.insert_run` / `report.generate` span is build-sequencing, not drift (obs-plan §4 still describes the intended instrumentation correctly; the bounded-span-name entry in §11 is added in the wiring epoch when the span is actually emitted). Generalizes the Foundation-epoch downstream-deferral rule above to Epoch-4 fault helpers and Epoch-5 core primitives. The prior gap chunk (P-015) self-cleared the identical case; abrupt-silence over-fired on the `fault_duration_ms` tension. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-20 (abrupt-silence-fault wrap; D-obs-instrumentation warning → dismiss); broadened from conductor-faults to any-seam primitive on 2026-06-21 (operator-pause-orchestration wrap — D-obs-instrumentation re-fired proposing a `pause.resolve` span for `resolve_hold` in conductor-core; same deferred-span build-sequencing, dismissed; `hold.wait_resolve` reserved for Epoch 8). Re-confirmed 2026-06-21 (runs-db-index wrap — D-obs-instrumentation proposed clarifying obs §4 that the `db.insert_run` span for `RunsDb::insert` (conductor-report) is deferred; dismissed as build-sequencing — obs §4 already describes the intended span, the §11 bounded-span-name entry lands with the Epoch-8 cli/timeline caller). Re-confirmed 2026-06-21 (markdown-run-report wrap — D-obs-instrumentation proposed clarifying obs §4 that the `report.generate` span for `RunReport::render`/`::write` (conductor-report) is deferred to the Epoch-8 cli/timeline caller; dismissed — the report primitive has no driver yet, obs §4 already names `report.generate`). **SPENT 2026-08-16 (fingerprint-storm-live-proof wrap, founder-ratified): the three fault spans — `fault.silence` / `fault.ramp` / `fault.port_occupier` — LEAVE the deferred list.** They were wired at `2026-08-16-fault-application-spans` and now emit (`fault.silence`/`fault.ramp` from `conductor-timeline`'s per-phase observer with `conductor-run` supplying the fault semantics; `fault.port_occupier` RAII in `conductor-faults` across `occupy`→`release`), so the dismiss no longer applies to them: a D-obs-instrumentation proposal about a fault span is now a GENUINE proposal to evaluate on its merits, not a build-sequencing dismiss. The any-seam-primitive CLASS stays live for the still-deferred `hold.wait_resolve` (Epoch 8 driver) and `db.insert_run` / `report.generate` (callers pending).

title: a drift detector (D-arch-decisions / similar) flags a TEST-ONLY use of a library feature the spec narrows to a productio
body:
- pattern: a drift detector (D-arch-decisions / similar) flags a TEST-ONLY use of a library feature the spec narrows to a production scope (e.g. rmcp `server` in a feature-gated `[[bin]]` or a dev-dependency), where the report shows it is never compiled into a default/release build and the production posture is unchanged
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — test fixtures are exempt from the production architecture posture; a feature-gated stub server (or a dev-dep `server` feature) that never ships does not make Conductor "a server". Precedent: chunk 1 (mcp-read-back-client) added rmcp `server` as a DEV-dependency for the in-proc `StubPulse` with no arch amendment; this chunk only promotes the same mock to a feature-gated `[[bin]] stub_pulse_mcp` (spawnable as a real child for the live preflight test). Arch §Stack already lists rmcp + §Infrastructure Patterns the dev-test stack; arch deliberately omits test-fixture mechanics (same reasoning as the D-arch-resources library-symbol over-reach rule). Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-21 (preflight-readiness-gate wrap; D-arch-decisions warning → dismiss).

title: a drift detector whose TRIGGER keys on the report
body:
- pattern: a drift detector whose TRIGGER keys on the report — a plan↔plan-bind detector (e.g. D-tests-obs-harness / D-a11y-obs-schema) whose precondition is unmet, OR a token-keyed cross-doc detector (D-platform-claim, and any check that greps a doc for a token the report names) — fires on a site the chunk's report shows it did NOT introduce (the chunk changed neither bound section), or on a site that merely MENTIONS the token without stating a claim of the detector's class (a descriptive mention, an entry-point pointer, an enumeration — not a verdict); the gap, where one exists at all, is pre-existing (often already a carried follow-up)
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — NOT this chunk's drift. The report is the single source of what changed; a plan↔plan bind detector whose precondition ("if the report changes the harness / status-read / log format / schema") is unmet has mis-fired on a pre-existing inconsistency that is out of scope this wrap and belongs to a dedicated doc-reconcile pass. Generalizes the not-added-dependency / library-symbol over-reach / deferred-span dismiss rules to plan↔plan bind detectors. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-21 (markdown-run-report wrap; D-tests-obs-harness fired proposing a test-plan §3 two-record-shapes clarification — the chunk only renders the existing RunRecord envelope to Markdown, touching neither §3; the test-plan §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 reconcile stays a carried follow-up). **Extended 2026-09-05 (0-pending adaptation, operator-directed): widened beyond plan↔plan-bind detectors.** At the 2026-09-04T17-15-00 wrap D-platform-claim fired ×3 on design-system sites that NAME the two-shell harness without stating any platform verdict, and the escalation found NO rule matched because this pattern named plan↔plan-bind detectors only (`fanout-results.md:28-29`); the operator dismissed all three by hand. The detector's own invariant was tightened the same day (drift-base D-platform-claim: the trigger is a STATING sentence, quoted in the proposal), so the shape now has a narrower trigger AND this dismissal rule. The dismissal never covers a site that STATES the retired claim — that is the drift the detector exists for.

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering individual scenario config FILES under `scenarios/` (or other per-item content wit
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering individual scenario config FILES under `scenarios/` (or other per-item content within an already-registered directory — INCLUDING read-back / detector-output TOKENS declared in a scenario's `[[expected]]`, e.g. `RetryStorm` / `ErrorRateSpike` / `ServiceWentSilent`) as occupied resources, where the directory + config-file category is already registered (arch §Cross-cutting [Config management] + §Infrastructure directory tree) and the chunk added no new port/socket/endpoint/IPC/event/env-var/crate
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the per-file/per-item flavor of the library-symbol rule above. arch registers `scenarios/` as a config-file CATEGORY (§Cross-cutting [Config management] "declarative scenario config files (serde + garde, no DSL)" + the §Infrastructure directory tree + CLAUDE.md §Key directories); the per-P-ID `.toml` files are CONTENT within that already-registered directory, not new occupied resources (the detector's own enumerated list is ports/sockets/endpoints/IPC/events/env-vars/crates — not config files, which arch tracks at directory grain). The category predates this chunk (Epoch-2 error-baseline-spike.toml registered none). Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-21 (connection-lifecycle-scenarios wrap; D-arch-resources fired proposing the 4 P-001..P-004 TOMLs into §Occupied Resources §On-disk artifacts). Prevents re-fire across the remaining Epoch-7 scenario chunks, each of which adds more scenario TOMLs. Broadened to read-back / detector-output TOKENS on 2026-06-22 (fingerprint-storm-scenarios wrap; D-arch-resources fired proposing the inferred `RetryStorm` token into §Occupied Resources — same over-reach: arch tracks the read-back contract at the 4 MCP tool names (§Occupied Resources) + the run-report envelope SHAPE (§Standard Contracts), NOT the open-ended detector-output token vocabulary; the 11 prior tokens — ErrorRateSpike/ServiceWentSilent/RestartEvent/LatencyRegression/ReceiverFailed/Idle/Stalled/Receiving/ERROR/WARN/exception — were never registered, and the chunk added no new port/socket/endpoint/IPC/event/env-var/crate). Pre-empts re-fire on severity-lifecycle (`Autonomous`/`Resolved`/`Curious`), constellation, and scrub/pipeline.

title: D-arch-decisions (or similar) flags a statistical-anomaly / baseline scenario declaring a `CountAtLeast` sample-count fl
body:
- pattern: D-arch-decisions (or similar) flags a statistical-anomaly / baseline scenario declaring a `CountAtLeast` sample-count floor (or a threshold-detection candidate) as `class=Hard` as contradicting arch §Probabilistic-Assertion Policy ("sample-count floors route to the calibration-region bucket instead of hard-failing")
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — no new decision; the chunk USES the pre-existing `CountAtLeast` mechanism (the kind + the `class` field + the evaluator override built in verdict-assertion-policy-split / expected-outcome-slo-timing-model). `class=Hard` is the DECLARED assertion policy for a MET floor (a hard pass); `conductor-verify::slo` (`slo.rs:79`) routes an UNMET `CountAtLeast` to the calibration-region, so arch's "floors route to calibration instead of hard-failing" already holds — the declared `class=Hard` and the evaluator's unmet→calibration override are COMPLEMENTARY, not contradictory. arch §Timing-Tolerance Model already NAMES the sample-count floors (50-sample latency / 10-span error-rate) and §Probabilistic-Assertion Policy already classifies "baseline math" as Hard; the proposed re-wording would also conflate `class` (declared) with `kind` (CountAtLeast/Contains). No arch edit. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-22 (error-baseline-spike-latency-regression-scenarios wrap; D-arch-decisions warning → dismiss). Prevents re-fire on ch4 activity-floor (P-013..P-016) + ch5 fingerprint-storm (P-017/P-018), which reuse floors/thresholds.

title: D-obs-instrumentation (or another §4-must-trace detector) fires on a SCENARIO-CONFIG chunk (a new `scenarios/*.toml` who
body:
- pattern: D-obs-instrumentation (or another §4-must-trace detector) fires on a SCENARIO-CONFIG chunk (a new `scenarios/*.toml` whose scenario name maps to an obs §4 must-trace path — e.g. restart-suppression), where the chunk adds the declarative TOML + fixture tests but NO runtime operation symbol (the spans are the Epoch-8 timeline/driver's to emit), and the report leaks nothing
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — the must-trace OPERATION is the live scenario UNDER the Epoch-8 driver (the emit/verify/report spans the driver emits), NOT the declarative TOML; a scenario-config chunk adds the structure, not the traced op, so the detector's "new must-trace operations the chunk adds" precondition is unmet. obs §4 correctly describes the TARGET instrumentation (forward-looking, written in target-state present tense throughout); the §11 bounded-span-name entry lands in the wiring epoch when the span is actually emitted — peppering §4 with per-epoch "not yet" caveats is noise the next scenario chunk re-triggers. The per-config-chunk flavor of the seam-primitive deferred-span rule above (which broadened conductor-faults → any-seam primitive); this broadens it once more to scenario-config chunks. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-22 (activity-floor-restart-suppression-scenarios wrap; D-obs-instrumentation warning on the restart-suppression must-trace path → dismiss). Pre-empts re-fire on the remaining Epoch-7 scenario chunks (fingerprint-storm P-017/P-018, severity-lifecycle, constellation, scrub/pipeline) whose scenarios map to obs §4 must-trace paths.

title: an escalate-severity security/obs boundary detector (D-security-input / D-security-subprocess / D-obs-redaction) demands
body:
- pattern: an escalate-severity security/obs boundary detector (D-security-input / D-security-subprocess / D-obs-redaction) demands re-confirmation of a hardening/validation invariant that the chunk CONSUMES from already-shipped, UNCHANGED infrastructure (conductor-core `resolve_under` path-guard · conductor-verify `ReadbackClient::connect` hardened sidecar spawn · conductor-core `init_observability` field-allowlist+scrub layer), where the chunk added NO new external-input boundary / spawn / logging-or-artifact path of its own
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — consuming shipped hardened infra is not a new boundary; the detector's precondition ("the chunk adds a new external-input surface / touches the sidecar spawn / adds a logging-or-artifact path") is unmet. The chunk wires EXISTING, unchanged seam APIs: `resolve_under` IS the §Input-Validation canonicalize + `..`/absolute/symlink-escape guard (config_path.rs); `ReadbackClient::connect` IS the §Anti-Patterns fixed-path + `.env(...)` + metachar-reject spawn (conductor-verify, crate-private helpers, untouched); `init_observability` installs the §6/§11 field-allowlist + value-scrub layer (obs.rs) the CLI inherits, and the persisted RunRecord envelope is path-free by construction. The invariant holds via the consumed infra; no new boundary ⇒ no new validation/hardening to add. The escalate-severity false-positive analogue of the not-added-dependency / library-symbol / deferred-span dismiss rules above (those are warning-severity over-reach; this is the boundary-detector escalate flavor — same "report is the single source of what changed; consuming unchanged hardened infra is not drift"). Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-23 (conductor-run-suite-report-verbs wrap; D-security-input demanded canonicalize [satisfied by resolve_under], D-security-subprocess demanded spawn confirmation [unchanged ReadbackClient::connect], D-obs-redaction claimed edge-only redaction [init_observability's layer + path-free envelope] — all 3 dismissed; `cargo audit` exit 0 verified the real new dep clap). Pre-empts re-fire on the remaining Epoch-8 CLI chunks (ch2–ch5) + Epoch-9 Tauri, which consume these same hardened entry points.

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering a new `conductor <verb>` CLI subcommand (or its `--flag`) into arch §Occupied Reso
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering a new `conductor <verb>` CLI subcommand (or its `--flag`) into arch §Occupied Resources / §Standard Contracts, where the chunk added no new port/socket/endpoint/IPC/event/env-var/crate and the verb belongs in layout-templates §cli Primary screens
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the CLI-verb flavor of the library-symbol + config-file over-reach rules above. arch §Occupied Resources tracks ports/sockets/endpoints/IPC/events/env-vars/crates + §Standard Contracts the readiness-gate / run-report-envelope SHAPES; the CLI VERB SURFACE is layout-templates' concern (§cli Primary screens), not arch's — run/suite/report/preflight were never registered in arch §Occupied Resources, and preflight (ch2) + coverage (this chunk) landed as layout-templates amendments. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-23 (line-oriented-output-rendering wrap; D-arch-resources proposed `conductor coverage` + the render module's public fns into §Occupied Resources — the verb went to layout-templates §cli, the render API is the library-symbol over-reach). Pre-empts re-fire on Epoch-8 ch4/ch5 (more verbs/flags) + Epoch-9 Tauri commands.

title: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a CLI PRESENTATION/render verb (e.g. `conductor coverage` / the `report` table render) by
body:
- pattern: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a CLI PRESENTATION/render verb (e.g. `conductor coverage` / the `report` table render) by matching it to an obs §4 must-trace path that actually belongs to a different VERIFICATION/GATE operation (e.g. the coverage-matrix COMPLETENESS gate, shipped 2026-09-06 as the `conductor-report --test coverage_gate` target), where the render verb does neither the DB query nor the validation assertion and leaks nothing
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — the must-trace OPERATION is the live verification/gate (which queries + asserts), NOT the presentation render of static in-code data; `conductor coverage` renders `coverage_matrix()` (a static classification — no DB query, no completeness assertion), so the obs §4 Critical-Path-6 spans belong to the Epoch-10 completeness gate, not this verb. The CLI-render flavor of the deferred-span rules above (seam-primitive / scenario-config): the traced op ships with its driver, not with the presentation. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-23 (line-oriented-output-rendering wrap; D-obs-instrumentation conflated the coverage render verb with the then-unbuilt completeness gate). Pre-empts re-fire on Epoch-8 ch4/ch5 rendering. **Updated 2026-09-06 (coverage-completeness-gate, operator-approved):** the gate SHIPPED, so the clause "obs §4 stays target-state" is retired — §4's Critical Path 6 was re-based onto the shipped shape in the same wrap, and the three span names this rule used to name the gate by (`report.coverage_matrix_generate` / `db.query_all_p_ids` / `report.validate_coverage`) were retired as never-built and unbuildable (outside §11's bounded set; their attributes absent from `ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS`). The dismissal itself stands, with one measured nuance: the gate's ASSERTION is the test target, but its OBSERVABLE necessarily sits on the render path (`conductor_report::coverage_rollup`) — a test binary emits no self-obs — so "the traced op ships with its driver" bounds which SPANS a render verb owes, never whether a render-path function may carry a boundary `info!`.

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering a Tauri framework capability PERMISSION (`core:window:allow-*` or any `core:<modul
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering a Tauri framework capability PERMISSION (`core:window:allow-*` or any `core:<module>:allow-*` ACL grant in `capabilities/*.json`) into arch §Occupied Resources / §Standard Contracts, where the chunk added no new Conductor `#[tauri::command]` / `Channel` / port / socket / endpoint / env-var / crate
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the Tauri-capability-perm flavor of the CLI-verb/command + library-symbol + config-file over-reach rules above. The `core:window:*` perms are FRAMEWORK window ops the deny-by-default ACL allows (security-plan §Tauri GUI's domain — the security detector validates the ACL there), NOT Conductor's own IPC methods; arch §Occupied Resources tracks Conductor's command surface (start/stop, scenario/suite picker, run-report, operator-pause + the one `Channel`), which this chunk did not touch. The `capabilities/*.json` file is config CONTENT within the already-registered `conductor-tauri` crate (the per-file flavor of the scenario-TOML rule). Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-24 (frameless-window-shell wrap; D-arch-resources proposed `core:window:allow-start-dragging`/`-minimize`/`-close` into §Occupied Resources — the genuine new resource was the `logs/conductor-tauri.jsonl` artifact, registered; the perms dismissed). Pre-empts re-fire on the remaining Epoch-9 Tauri chunks (picker / Channel / operator-pause dialog), each adding more capability perms.

title: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a frontend call to a Tauri BUILT-IN framework command (e.g. `getCurrentWindow().minimize(
body:
- pattern: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a frontend call to a Tauri BUILT-IN framework command (e.g. `getCurrentWindow().minimize()/.close()` via `@tauri-apps/api`, gated by a `core:window:*` capability) demanding a `#[tracing::instrument]` span, where the chunk implements NO Conductor `#[tauri::command]` handler of its own and leaks nothing
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — the must-trace OPERATION is Conductor's OWN live command handler (the obs §4 `tauri.command.*` spans ship WITH the start/stop/picker/operator-pause handlers in later Epoch-9 chunks), NOT a frontend call into Tauri's framework-internal window IPC (minimize/close are handled BY Tauri, not Conductor). The Tauri-framework-op flavor of the deferred-span family above (seam-primitive / scenario-config / CLI-render): the traced op ships with Conductor's driver, not with a framework call; obs §4 stays target-state. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-24 (frameless-window-shell wrap; D-obs-instrumentation demanded instrumentation on the minimize/close window controls — no Conductor command handler exists this chunk). Pre-empts re-fire on the remaining Epoch-9 Tauri chunks until the command/`Channel` handlers land.

title: D-arch-resources / D-arch-decisions proposes registering a Conductor `#[tauri::command]` NAME (e.g. list_scenarios / sta
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources / D-arch-decisions proposes registering a Conductor `#[tauri::command]` NAME (e.g. list_scenarios / start_run / stop_run), an internal MODULE within an already-registered crate (e.g. conductor-tauri::commands, conductor-core::scenario_catalog), or a frontend COMPONENT PACKAGE / component-styling decision (e.g. cmdk — shadcn Command's engine) into arch §Occupied Resources / §Stack / §Established Decisions, where the chunk added no new port / socket / endpoint / env-var / crate
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the Tauri-command-name + internal-module + frontend-component-package flavor of the established library-symbol / CLI-verb / Tauri-capability-perm / config-file over-reach family. arch §Occupied Resources registers the Tauri command surface at CATEGORY grain ("Tauri commands (internal IPC): start/stop, scenario/suite picker, run-report view, operator-pause prompt; one `Channel`") — the concrete handler fn names (list_scenarios/start_run/stop_run) are the realization arch omits, exactly as it omits per-crate public symbols + CLI verb names. Internal modules (commands / scenario_catalog) are content within already-registered crates, NOT workspace members (§Crate names lists members). The frontend component-library decision lives in design-system §Component Patterns §5 ("shadcn Command/Select (Radix-driven)") + frontend.md — arch §Stack summarizes the frontend stack (React/Vite/Tailwind) and never enumerated shadcn/Radix/Lucide; cmdk is the impl of the already-locked shadcn-Command decision (recorded in package.json + gated by npm audit), and frontend-component-styling is below the altitude of an arch §Established Decision (which locks language / runtime / DB / module-boundaries) — its realization (cmdk-direct + token `.css`) is a frontend.md curation learning, not an arch lock. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-26 (scenario-suite-picker-start-stop wrap; D-arch-resources proposed the 3 command names + the conductor-tauri/conductor-core modules + cmdk-into-§Stack, D-arch-decisions proposed a cmdk Established Decision — all dismissed; the genuine new surfaces map to the pre-registered command category + the design-system component decision, validated boundaries [validate_selection/resolve_under], and audit-green deps). Pre-empts re-fire on Epoch-9 ch4 (Channel command), ch5 (component primitives library), ch8 (operator-pause dialog command).

title: a GUI-integration-tier test detector (D-tests-coverage / D-a11y-surface) flags a Tauri `#[tauri::command]` / `Channel` h
body:
- pattern: a GUI-integration-tier test detector (D-tests-coverage / D-a11y-surface) flags a Tauri `#[tauri::command]` / `Channel` handler for lacking a `tauri::test` mock-runtime (or tauri-driver webview) test, where the chunk drives the command's logic on a BACKGROUND THREAD streaming the Channel asynchronously (so an in-process frame-sequence assertion is thread-timing-dependent — it flakes against the zero-retry bar), the run/handler LOGIC is covered deterministically at a library unit tier (e.g. conductor-run drive_run) + the CLI parity E2E, and the GUI test harness (tauri-driver) is an explicitly route-sequenced later chunk
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss/document — the Tauri-command WRAPPER (thread + Channel plumbing + path resolution) is glue; its substantive logic is the library fn it calls, which IS unit-tested deterministically, and the GUI integration leg (mock-runtime frame assertion + webview parity) belongs to the sequenced tauri-driver/a11y-harness chunk — deferring it is build-sequencing against a hard project invariant (zero-flakiness; no nextest retries), not a coverage gap, when the report shows the logic covered + the CLI parity E2E green. The GUI-test flavor of the Foundation/seam-primitive/scenario-config deferral family (those defer obs spans; this defers the GUI integration test). Document the deferral in test-plan §5; do NOT re-open implement to force a flaky thread-timing test. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-26 (live-counter-channel-stream wrap; D-tests-coverage fired on the start_run/stop_run + cross-surface-parity tauri::test — the run logic is covered by conductor-run drive_run unit tests + cli_smoke parity, the GUI leg defers to the tauri-driver harness chunk). Pre-empts re-fire on Epoch-9 ch5 (component primitives) + ch8 (operator-pause dialog), whose Tauri command/Channel handlers face the same async-stream testability constraint.

title: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a read-only Tauri query `#[tauri::command]` (e.g. list_scenarios / coverage_matrix) that
body:
- pattern: D-obs-instrumentation fires on a read-only Tauri query `#[tauri::command]` (e.g. list_scenarios / coverage_matrix) that carries the established `tauri.command.<name>` manual span + `info!(count, latency_ms)` boundary line but no `run_id`, where the command executes OUTSIDE any scenario run and the chunk introduces no new instrumentation pattern of its own
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — not drift. obs §6's "run_id on every line" governs the SCENARIO-RUN self-obs stream (where a run_id exists); a read-only query command (scenario/suite picker, coverage matrix) runs outside any run and legitimately has none. The pattern shipped with `list_scenarios` (scenario-suite-picker-start-stop, ch3) and is documented in observability.md (manual `tauri.command.*` span + `count`/`latency_ms`, both allowlisted; `sanitize_error` edge). A later read-only command consuming that SAME unchanged pattern introduces no new drift (the report-is-single-source / consuming-established-infra family), and the detector's proposed synthetic run_id (`query-<op>-<ISO>`) would itself create a NEW inconsistency vs `list_scenarios`. The read-only-query-command flavor of the consuming-shipped-infra (2026-06-23) + plan↔plan not-introduced (2026-06-21) dismiss rules. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-27 (coverage-matrix-view wrap; D-obs-instrumentation fired on `coverage_matrix`'s run_id-less `info!` line). Pre-empts re-fire on Epoch-9 ch7 (run-report view) + ch8 (operator-pause command) read-only query commands. Re-confirmed 2026-06-27 (operator-pause-go-no-go-dialog wrap; D-obs-instrumentation fired on `resolve_operator_hold`'s run_id-less span — a stateless decision-post outside any run, same pattern; dismissed, NOT a §3 exemption amendment).

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering an additional IPC `Channel` INSTANCE (a 2nd `tauri::ipc::Channel<T>` carrying a di
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering an additional IPC `Channel` INSTANCE (a 2nd `tauri::ipc::Channel<T>` carrying a distinct backend→frontend stream, e.g. the operator-hold prompt) into arch §Occupied Resources / §Real-time Strategy / §Standard Contracts, where the stream serves an already-registered command/surface CATEGORY (e.g. "operator-pause prompt") and the chunk added no new port / socket / endpoint / env-var / crate
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the IPC-transport-INSTANCE flavor of the Tauri-command-name (2026-06-26) + library-symbol / CLI-verb / capability-perm / config-file over-reach family. arch §Occupied Resources registers the Tauri command/stream surface at CATEGORY grain ("...operator-pause prompt; one `Channel` for live counters") — the concrete TRANSPORT of an already-registered surface (a handler fn name, OR the `Channel` instance carrying its prompt) is the realization arch omits. The existing "one `Channel` for live counters" stays TRUE (the live-counter Channel still exists; the new Channel carries prompts, not counters — it does not contradict the statement). The operator-pause prompt was a registered surface from the start; ch8 only realized its transport as a 2nd `Channel` + the `resolve_operator_hold` command (command name dismissed per 2026-06-26; the Channel dismissed here). Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-27 (operator-pause-go-no-go-dialog wrap; D-arch-resources proposed both into §Occupied Resources). Pre-empts re-fire on any future chunk adding a `Channel` for an already-registered surface.

title: D-security-deps (escalate) fires on new npm devDependencies in `crates/conductor-tauri/ui` (non-shipping test/build tool
body:
- pattern: D-security-deps (escalate) fires on new npm devDependencies in `crates/conductor-tauri/ui` (non-shipping test/build tooling — e.g. the a11y harness lighthouse/webdriverio/axe/colorjs.io/@crabnebula/tauri-driver tree) whose ONLY `npm audit` findings are dev-only + transitive (not fixable non-breaking), where `npm audit --omit=dev` = 0 (no production vulnerability) and the tooling never ships in any binary
  verdict: routine
  note: apply the dev-aware-gate amendment — gate on `npm audit --omit=dev` (production deps strictly clean) + accept dev-only transitive advisories at dev-tree grain, the npm analogue of the established deny.toml accepted-exceptions mechanism (security.md 2026-06-23/24; cargo uses per-advisory `[advisories] ignore`, npm uses the category-grain `--omit=dev` — chosen for a Minimal-tier local tool to avoid adding an audit-suppression tool). DISTINCT from the npm-audit-driven PRODUCTION bump (design-token-typography-bundle: Vite 6→8 cleared a real production esbuild advisory) — that floor discipline still applies to production deps; only NON-SHIPPING DEV advisories are accepted. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-27 (desktop-a11y-harness-setup wrap; implement chose "Dev-aware gate", wrap chose the `--omit=dev` mechanism over a granular suppression tool; 20 dev-only advisories via lighthouse→@sentry/node→@opentelemetry/core + @wdio/mocha-framework→mocha→serialize-javascript, none fixable non-breaking, `--omit=dev`=0). security-plan §Dependency Security now states the dev-aware gate; ci.yml runs `npm audit --omit=dev`. Pre-empts re-fire on the Epoch-9 a11y-verification chunk + any future chunk adding non-shipping npm dev tooling.

title: a chunk that OPERATIONALIZES a spec'd CI gate / verification step for the FIRST time surfaces that the SAME spec's own d
body:
- pattern: a chunk that OPERATIONALIZES a spec'd CI gate / verification step for the FIRST time surfaces that the SAME spec's own description of that gate names a stale/wrong record-shape, field-list, or artifact (e.g. obs §9's `agent-latest.jsonl` conformance pointing at the §6 run-report ENVELOPE instead of the §3 self-obs BASE set), where the shipped gate follows the CANONICAL definition elsewhere in the spec and the report shows the gate passes
  verdict: routine
  note: apply the spec-wording→sound-impl reconciliation (the established 2026-06-15 rule), scoped to the OPERATIONALIZING doc's OWN section — the chunk that first BUILDS the gate the spec describes is exactly the chunk whose "current truth" now includes the gate's real behavior, so reconciling the spec's own stale description to the canonical record shape is bringing the body to current truth, not introducing drift. Intra-doc (obs §9 → obs §3 line 229 "two record shapes") needs no cross-plan owner — test-plan §3 OWNS the run-report ENVELOPE schema and was already correct; obs §9 merely mis-referenced §6 for an artifact (`agent-latest.jsonl`) that carries the §3 base set. DISTINCT from the 2026-06-21 "dismiss a pre-existing cross-PLAN-bind inconsistency the chunk did NOT introduce" rule: there the chunk changed NEITHER bound section (a dedicated reconcile pass owns it); here the chunk OPERATIONALIZED the gate, engaging the section substantively. Escalated (not silent-applied) on first occurrence due to the record-shape sensitivity (a long-flagged §3↔§3 follow-up); confirmed with the user on 2026-06-27 (obs-ci-conformance-gate wrap; obs §9 conformance field-list §6-envelope → §3-base). Pre-empts re-fire when the Epoch-10 envelope/A11y CI conformance gates operationalize their own spec'd checks.

title: an external supply-chain input DECAYS under a STATIC dependency tree
body:
- pattern: an external supply-chain input DECAYS under a STATIC dependency tree — a new advisory appears against an unchanged tree, OR the advisory database itself fails to parse/fetch — making a supply-chain gate RED while the chunk's own dependency delta is zero and the OVERLAPPING gate stays green
  verdict: routine
  note: record a BOUNDED DEFERRAL; do not distort the project. External decay is not the chunk's drift — the report's Dependencies bullet is the single source of what changed, and a zero-delta chunk with un-drifted lockfiles cannot have caused it. The response is bounded, and it FORKS on which of the two faults it is (established 2026-08-09, `2026-08-09-interpretation-correctness-posture`): a **TOOL fault** (the scanner is too old / carries a fixed bug) → re-check at the NEXT chunk and if it persists raise the tool's FLOOR to the fixed release (security-plan §Dependency Security states floors, not pins — the 2026-06-15 rule above already establishes that dev CLI tools can't be pinned in `Cargo.lock`); an **advisory-DATABASE fault** (the DB itself will not parse/fetch, so NO released version can read it) → the floor raise is UNEXECUTABLE and would look like compliance while changing nothing, so the remedy is the bounded WAIT alone, re-checked each chunk, with the audit↔deny overlap VERIFIED green rather than assumed. Prove which fault it is before prescribing — and prove FIRST that the data under test is the WORLD's: a measurement of an external artifact reads its CURRENT state (`git status --porcelain` empty in the local advisory-db checkout, or a fresh clone into an empty location / a CI run's clean checkout); a fetch INTO an existing copy does not clear residue, so a byte-identical local signature is evidence of a stable CACHE until that check has run — only then does the fork apply: install the latest published tool and re-run — identical failure means the data, not the tool (2026-08-09: `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244` failed byte-identically on 0.22.1 and on the latest 0.22.2, read then as committed data in the advisory-db — **corrected 2026-09-05 (0-pending adaptation, operator-directed): it was NOT; upstream had moved that file from `crates/gettext-sys/` to `crates/gettext-rs/` on 2026-08-09, the deferral's first day, and the duplicate was an untracked leftover in the LOCAL `$CARGO_HOME/advisory-db` checkout whose HEAD matched upstream throughout — 52 consecutive identical readings were the cache's, not the world's; CI's clean checkout passed the same step and a fresh `--db` clone exits 0. The seeded playbook template carries the same current-state clause**). Explicitly NOT: a `deny.toml` ignore entry (that suppresses a real signal CLASS for a transient external fault), NOT a CI edit, NOT a silent accept. What preserves the signal meanwhile is the deliberate audit+deny OVERLAP (security.md 2026-06-23: the gate MUST run both) — one going red for an external reason while the other is green is the overlap working as designed, not a hole. DISTINCT from the 2026-06-15 tool-version-lag rule above, whose trigger is a GREEN gate on a slightly-behind tool; this rule's trigger is a RED gate from decay outside the project. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-09 (out-of-scope-classification-treatment wrap; `cargo audit` exit 1 on "error loading advisory database: parse error: duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244" — the RustSec DB itself would not parse, reproduced identically with a fresh fetch and with `-n` against the cache; zero dependency delta, both lockfiles un-drifted, `cargo deny check` advisories/bans/licenses/sources all ok). Second occurrence of the class: 2026-08-08-dependency-advisory-remediation was the advisory-appears-against-a-static-tree flavor (lock-only bumps cleared RUSTSEC-2026-0194/-0195/-0204 with no Tauri bump). Note the CI consequence when this fires: CI's own `cargo audit` step hits the same wall until upstream heals — that is part of what the deferral tracks. The converse is the discriminator: CI GREEN while the local probe stays red means the fault is LOCAL (measured 2026-09-05 — run 33954347685 passed `cargo audit` on a clean checkout while the local cache reproduced the old signature).

title: D-security-input (or another security detector) proposes adding a new Conductor `#[tauri::command]` NAME to security-pla
body:
- pattern: D-security-input (or another security detector) proposes adding a new Conductor `#[tauri::command]` NAME to security-plan §Threat Model's Tauri-IPC attack-surface enumeration ("internal in-app commands (`#[tauri::command]` start/stop/picker/run-report/operator-pause) + one `Channel`"), where the command is nullary/read-only (adds no operator-input boundary) and the chunk added no new port / socket / endpoint / env-var / crate
  verdict: routine
  note: dismiss — over-reach, the SECURITY-PLAN flavor of the 2026-06-26 arch command-name over-reach rule (this rule family was scoped to arch's registries; the same misfire lands here). That enumeration is CATEGORY-grain and illustrative, not an allowlist: it already omits `coverage_matrix` (shipped 2026-06-27 ch6) and never tracked `resolve_operator_hold` by name, and the "a capabilities author must allow only the enumerated commands" argument is factually wrong for app commands — security.md 2026-06-26 established that `#[tauri::command]`s registered via `invoke_handler`/`generate_handler!` are NOT capability-ACL-gated (only `core:`/plugin permissions are). The real security boundary is the command's INPUT validation, which a nullary const-returning query does not have. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-09 (interpretation-correctness-posture wrap; D-security-input escalate on `unbacked_auto` → dismiss + this rule). Pre-empts re-fire on every future read-only Tauri command.

title: a chunk REVERSES a locked arch §Established Decision because the live SUT's actual behavior contradicts it (a tech choic
body:
- pattern: a chunk REVERSES a locked arch §Established Decision because the live SUT's actual behavior contradicts it (a tech choice that proved unworkable against the real system), user-confirmed at /andromeda-phase P4, where the report shows the decision's INVARIANTS still hold via the replacement (only the mechanism changed)
  verdict: escalate
  note: escalate once to ratify the reversal + apply the arch amendment (body → the new decision in current truth; the superseded rationale → the architecture-amendments sidecar), then the consequential same-reversal mentions across the doc (Stack/Conventions/Inherited/tree + any security/test/obs prose naming the old tech) reconcile in lockstep as routine wording→current-truth (the invariants preserved). DISTINCT from the 2026-06-15 spec-illustration→sound-impl rule (that aligns wording/mechanism WITHIN a decision; this REVERSES the decision's choice — hence escalate, not silent). The user's P4 approach-confirmation + the surfaced spec↔reality gap that drove the re-plan ARE the resolution; the wrap escalation is the conscious ratify-the-arch-record step, not a re-litigation. Confirmed with the user on 2026-06-27 (mcp-read-back-result-shape-adapter wrap; arch [MCP Read-Back Client] rmcp → hand-rolled JSON-RPC because Pulse's `tools/call` is non-MCP-compliant — rmcp's typed `call_tool` `UnexpectedResponse`'d every live call; the negotiate-down + hardened spawn + bounded decode invariants all held). Pre-empts a future live-SUT-forced locked-decision reversal from re-deriving the whole escalation from scratch.

title: a chunk lands a NEW committed, runtime-parsed config artifact under `contracts/` (read at a fixed `default_path()` throu
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW committed, runtime-parsed config artifact under `contracts/` (read at a fixed `default_path()` through `resolve_under`, deliberately with no `CONDUCTOR_*` override handle), and a security detector proposes registering it as a §Input Validation boundary row
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — §Input Validation is an EXHAUSTIVE enumeration of external-input surfaces, so a genuinely new committed artifact parsed at runtime earns a row (what to validate + how). DISTINCT from the 2026-06-23 consuming-shipped-infra dismiss rule, whose precondition is explicitly "the chunk added NO new external-input boundary" — here the chunk added one; the dismiss rule covers a chunk merely *using* `resolve_under` / the hardened spawn / the redaction layer unchanged. Second occurrence of the class: `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml` (2026-08-08-sut-capability-manifest) and `contracts/pulse-load-envelope.toml` (2026-08-09-sut-load-envelope), both with identical controls (bounds-check at load · fixed path · no env override · `e.kind()`-only read faults · absent ⇒ hard fault, never defaulted). Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-10 (sut-load-envelope wrap; D-security-input escalate → apply + this rule). NOTE the trap this occurrence exposed: the 2026-08-08 sidecar recorded its row as landed while the BODY carried none — when applying, grep the body for the sibling artifact rather than trusting the sidecar, and widen the row to cover any sibling found missing.

title: a chunk lands a NEW dependency (a real `Cargo.lock` delta) while the supply-chain gate is red for an EXTERNAL advisory-D
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW dependency (a real `Cargo.lock` delta) while the supply-chain gate is red for an EXTERNAL advisory-DATABASE fault — the precondition of the bounded-deferral rule above ("the chunk's own dependency delta is zero") no longer holds
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — admit the dependency ONLY on a `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` VERIFIED green over the NEW lockfile (verified, never assumed), since the deny overlap is then the SOLE coverage for the added packages; any new license/advisory it surfaces takes the established justified-exception mechanism (a `[licenses] allow` / `[advisories] ignore` entry naming the crate and its dependency path). When re-pinning the deferral, STATE the changed basis. The form the pin returns to keys on whether the delta ADMITS A PACKAGE, not on whether `Cargo.lock` moved: a delta that admits one changes the very set `cargo deny` scans, so "no dependency delta" stops being available as a reason and the pin returns to FULL form; a delta that is EDGE-ONLY (a dependency-list line for a package already resolved in the tree, zero `[[package]]` nodes added or removed — verified by diff, never assumed) leaves deny's coverage set identical, so the COMPACT ratified form still stands, provided the deny-green verification below was actually run over the new lock. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-20 (`2026-08-20-read-back-seam-survivors-closed` wrap — first measured instance of the edge-only case: `assert_fs` added as a `conductor-verify` dev-dep, already a workspace dep consumed by `conductor-run`, one lock line, zero package nodes, deny true exit 0; this sharpening aligns the rule with the route PREREQ's own signature, which had already narrowed the trigger to "a dependency delta that ADMITS a package"). DISTINCT from the 2026-08-09 bounded-deferral rule above, which governs a ZERO-delta chunk (external decay is not that chunk's drift); this rule governs the case where the chunk genuinely changes the tree under a gate that cannot scan it. Explicitly NOT: blocking the chunk on an external fault (the deferral exists precisely because no floor can be raised), and NOT a `deny.toml` ignore standing in for the missing audit. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-16 (canary-fingerprint-derivation-aligned wrap; `blake3` 1.8.6 + `arrayref`/`arrayvec`/`constant_time_eq`/`cpufeatures` landed against the 22nd consecutive `duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`, with deny true exit 0 across all four classes after a justified BSD-2-Clause allow for `arrayref`). security-plan §Dependency Security now states the admission condition.

title: a D-{doc}-derived-count amendment fires on a doc SAMPLE whose own surrounding prose already declares the value manifest-
body:
- pattern: a D-{doc}-derived-count amendment fires on a doc SAMPLE whose own surrounding prose already declares the value manifest-derived (e.g. layout-templates §cli coverage roll-up caption: "every number manifest-derived (never a literal)"), and the prior occurrences each SUBSTITUTED a fresh literal that then re-staled
  verdict: routine
  note: apply as a DE-LITERALIZATION, never another substitution — replace the baked value with the doc's own placeholder form (`(N unbacked)`), so the sample stops contradicting the rule stated beside it and the amendment stops recurring. The detector's own `check` text already sanctions this ("the fix is always to name the set or update the sample, never to substitute a fresh literal that re-stales"); what this rule adds is WHEN to stop updating the sample and de-literalize instead — at the point the recurrence is established. Third occurrence of the identical amendment when ratified: `11 → 10` (2026-08-09-in-lane-sut-scenarios, P-079), `10 → 9` (2026-08-10-pulse-run-contract, P-073), `9 → 8` (2026-08-16-fingerprint-storm-live-proof, P-074). DISTINCT from a derived count in PROSE that names the set rather than a literal — that was never a hit. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-16 (fingerprint-storm-live-proof wrap; D-layout-derived-count warning → apply as de-literalization + this rule).

title: an obs drift detector attributes obs-plan §4's `#[tracing::instrument]` mandate to the **cli** row of the per-surface ta
body:
- pattern: an obs drift detector attributes obs-plan §4's `#[tracing::instrument]` mandate to the **cli** row of the per-surface table (line 48), and proposes an amendment because a crate's direct `tracing` edge changed
  verdict: escalate
  note: the mandate is NOT on the cli row — §4's cli row names "`tracing` 0.1.x crate + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter" as the surface's hook, while the MANUAL `tracing::info_span!("tauri.command.<name>").entered()` guard is mandated on the **desktop-webview** (:49) and **ipc-internal** (:50) rows, both about `#[tauri::command]` handlers (mechanism corrected 2026-09-01 — the `#[tracing::instrument]` ATTRIBUTE does not stack with the command macro, so those rows no longer name it). The cli row describes the SURFACE's mechanism, which `conductor-core`'s `init_observability` supplies — so removing a cli-crate `tracing` edge does not falsify it. Recurred TWICE on 2026-08-20 (the phase-time obs distiller and the wrap-time obs detector, same chunk); resolved with the user at the `2026-08-20-verifier-self-hardening` wrap. Verify the row's actual text before proposing.

title: a chunk lands a NEW declarative KEY inside an already-registered scenario-config artifact (a `[[table]]` or field under
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW declarative KEY inside an already-registered scenario-config artifact (a `[[table]]` or field under `scenarios/*.toml`), garde-validated at load, and D-security-input (or D-arch-resources) proposes registering it as a §Input Validation boundary / §Conventions config-key
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — §Input Validation is an EXHAUSTIVE enumeration of external-input surfaces, and §Conventions Config conventions is the arch-side registry of declarative keys, so a genuinely new key earns an entry in both. DISTINCT from the `contracts/` rule above, whose subject is a new committed ARTIFACT; this is a new key INSIDE an artifact already registered. Fourth occurrence of the class: `[phases.emission]`, `[[expected]].budget_ms`, `[phases.fault]`, and now `[[checklist]]` (2026-08-22-operator-pause-and-checklist-live-firing). When applying, ALSO widen any CLOSED `Scenario::check_*()` enumeration the key's sibling-spanning rule joins — those lists are restated in arch [Scenario Config Format] + [Validation Library] and in security-plan §Input Validation + §Threat Model, and a single-site apply leaves three stale. Confirmed with the user on 2026-08-22.

title: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` HOST-TOOL path handle read solely by `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` HOST-TOOL path handle read solely by `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` (never by a Conductor binary) behind the wdio-edge guard (existence + `isFile` + shell-metacharacter rejection), used only in an array-form spawn, skipping at exit 0 when unset, and the chunk's plan `Expected amendments (wrap)` list names the security-plan §Input Validation row — and D-security-input (escalate) proposes that row plus the widening of every singular "the one handle" clause
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — add the §Input Validation row and widen EVERY singular exception clause to the handle SET (Threat Model CLI-input vector · Bootstrap `input-validation-library-install` · Secret Management Development · Anti-Patterns Input canonicalize ban · the arch env-var registry's "one HOST dev-tool handle"), never a single-site apply. The boundary is genuinely new (a host path arriving by env) but its control is the shipped `UNSAFE_PATH` guard shape, so the detector's escalate severity is its default class rather than a finding; the operator ratified the mechanism at the plan's P5 card and the row on the plan's own list. Second occurrence of the class: `CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` (2026-09-01-webview-self-verify-windows-host) and `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` (2026-09-02-screen-reader-manual-spec). Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-02 (screen-reader-manual-spec wrap; approved as written on 2026-09-02).

title: an escalate-severity security/obs boundary detector (D-obs-redaction / D-security-subprocess / D-security-input) fires o
body:
- pattern: an escalate-severity security/obs boundary detector (D-obs-redaction / D-security-subprocess / D-security-input) fires on a MEASURED product DEFECT — a real leak or hardening gap the chunk measured but did not fix (zero delta at the defect's site) — that the operator's wrap directive has ALREADY dispositioned as a route candidate, NAMING THE DEFECT ITSELF (the site, the mechanism, the symptom), never a class of defects
  verdict: routine
  note: apply as a RECORD, never as a shipped control — the master's body states the measurement (`measured at {evidence}`), names the fix as route-owned and cites the directive; the governing ban or rule may gain the duty (e.g. "the sidecar spawn must also suppress its console window") so long as the same passage says it is not yet shipped. The escalate severity exists to stop a chunk hiding a leak; once the operator has named that exact defect and routed it, the substance is resolved and only the recording remains. A directive naming a CLASS ("spawn defects", "host-path leaks", "the a11y findings") satisfies nothing — the halt stays. First occurrence: the sidecar console-pane host-path disclosure (`conductor-verify/src/spawn.rs:80`, no creation flags; measured 2026-09-02 at the NVDA leg, SR pass row S1-01; D-obs-redaction ×2 + D-security-subprocess ×1). Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-02 (screen-reader-manual-spec wrap; approved with the "must NAME the defect, never a class" refinement on 2026-09-02).

title: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` handle whose value is a HARNESS-OWNED CONSTANT (not an operator-suppl
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` handle whose value is a HARNESS-OWNED CONSTANT (not an operator-supplied host path) — SET by `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` and READ by a `conductor-run` TEST binary rather than by wdio, never by a shipped binary, inert (a no-op) when unset — and D-security-input / D-arch-resources (escalate) propose the security-plan §Input Validation row, the arch env-var registry entry, and the widening of every singular "the two handles" clause
  verdict: routine
  note: apply as a THIRD handle class, distinct from BOTH shipped shapes, and widen every exhaustive clause to the SET of three with the reason SPLIT where it differs (`CONDUCTOR_MSEDGEDRIVER` / `CONDUCTOR_NVDA` never reach Rust at all; this class reaches Rust only in a TEST binary) — never a single-site apply. Its control model is neither of the others': the `std::fs::canonicalize` rule does not bind (no shipped binary reads it) and the wdio-edge `isFile` + shell-metacharacter guard has nothing to guard (the value is not operator input), so the §Input Validation row MUST record the residual explicitly — the repo-relative discipline lives at the wdio caller and holds only while no shipped binary reads the handle. The arch registry's "one of TWO handles naming a HOST dev-tool" clause stays TRUE and is left standing, because this handle names a path the document itself defines. Distinguish from the 2026-09-02 host-tool rule above, whose preconditions this class fails on four of five clauses (host-tool path · read solely by wdio · behind the isFile/metacharacter guard · named on the plan's expected-amendments list) — stretching that rule would widen a precedent whose guard shape this class does not share. First occurrence: `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` (2026-09-02-cross-surface-envelope-parity), which additionally contradicted its own chunk's plan acceptance criterion ("no new `CONDUCTOR_*` env var") — the intent-consistency divergence is ratified separately and does not travel with this rule. Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-02 (cross-surface-envelope-parity wrap; approved as written).

title: Boundary widening
body:
- pattern: Boundary widening — a chunk WIDENS what crosses an already-hardened boundary (a read-only channel gains a write, a validated surface admits a new input class, a subprocess/IPC boundary gains a new crossing) and the proposal records it.
  verdict: escalate
  note: always a human's call — never mint a routine rule for this class, however often it recurs: the recurrence is the reason it must keep reaching the operator (a routine verdict here silently widens a precedent). The escalation resolves on the operator's ratification, recorded in the sidecar.

title: a D-{doc}-derived-count amendment fires on a stale literal that ENUMERATES A SET the code owns (a CLI verb surface, a st
body:
- pattern: a D-{doc}-derived-count amendment fires on a stale literal that ENUMERATES A SET the code owns (a CLI verb surface, a status-label set, a term list), where the surrounding prose does NOT already declare the value derived AND no prior wrap substituted a fresh literal that then re-staled — i.e. the two qualifiers of the de-literalization rule above both fail
  verdict: routine
  note: apply as SET-NAMING — name the set by its source of truth (the enum / const / artifact the code owns) and never write a fresh count, which would re-stale on the next addition. This is the SIBLING of the de-literalization rule above, for the case where the recurrence has NOT yet been established: that rule waits for a doc to declare the value derived and for prior substitutions to have re-staled; this one fires the first time, because the remedy is identical and waiting only banks a second stale literal. Minted on 9 proposals across FOUR docs in one pass at 2026-09-03-live-pulse-preconditions-probed: the CLI verb surface 3 -> 6 (architecture Stack row, layout-templates Primary navigation + Decisions Log, a11y-plan §1 cli entity — the literal had been stale since `preflight` landed and no wrap ever updated it) and the cli run-level non-lamp label 1 -> 2 (design-system status-prefix line + ANSI-map reuse list, test-plan §1 Signal + §6 driver row + §6 Selector strategy). Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-03.

title: a chunk lands a NEW declarative key inside an already-registered, runtime-parsed config artifact under `contracts/` (a `
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW declarative key inside an already-registered, runtime-parsed config artifact under `contracts/` (a `[[term]]` / table / field in a manifest read at a fixed `default_path()` through `resolve_under`), and D-arch-resources or a security detector proposes registering it
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — the `scenarios/*.toml` new-key rule above and the new-`contracts/`-ARTIFACT rule above are the same registry logic at two grains, and this is the third: the artifact is already registered, so what earns an entry is the KEY. Register it where the artifact's own registry entry lives (arch §Occupied Resources) and, where the key names an external input, in security-plan §Input Validation — that section is an EXHAUSTIVE enumeration. DISTINCT from the artifact rule (whose subject is a whole new file) and from the scenarios rule (whose qualifier names `scenarios/*.toml` and so does not reach `contracts/`). First occurrence: the `mcp-enabled` `[[term]]` in `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml` (2026-09-03-live-pulse-preconditions-probed) — a `shell-declaration` term of the same class as the shipped `l4-deterministic`, needing no new machinery. Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-03.

title: a chunk SHIPS the fix that a spec master's own body already names as route-owned-not-shipped (the master records the def
body:
- pattern: a chunk SHIPS the fix that a spec master's own body already names as route-owned-not-shipped (the master records the defect, names the corrective route entry, and cites the measurement), and a detector proposes retiring that recorded defect in favour of the shipped fix — including at escalate severity
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — the master itself scoped the work and this chunk discharged it, so bringing the body to current truth is the amendment flow doing its job, not a judgment about widening. The amendment must carry the NEW measurement (the evidence pointer for the fix), state what it SUPERSEDES when a prior measured reading is cited elsewhere, and preserve every property the retired passage held that the fix did not touch. **Check rule `Boundary widening` FIRST and defer to it when it matches** — this rule covers a defect being CLOSED, never a boundary being WIDENED; the discriminator is whether anything new crosses a hardened boundary as a result. It did not here: the precondition probe grants no access and passes no value onward (a distinctive data-dir value appeared 0 times across every output arm), the gate that can BLOCK was behaviourally unchanged and structurally cannot reach the new grading arm, and security-plan's own withdrawn bullet had identified the PRE-fix state as the downgrade — so the chunk narrowed back to intent rather than past it. First occurrence: `2026-09-04-preconditions-probe-reads-path-handles-by-presence` (D-security-input ×3 retiring the "not a downgrade" withdrawal, the READ SET row and the spawn-row parenthetical; security-plan `:114`/`:120`/`:367`). Confirmed with the user on 2026-09-04 (escalation E1). **Extended 2026-09-23 (operator-approved at the `2026-09-23-real-model-capture-path-handles-guarded-and-stale-read-back-texts-corrected` wrap card): the route-entry clause is ALSO met when the master recorded the defect as a residual but never routed it, and the operator's RECORDED /andromeda-phase P4 scope ruling brought it into the chunk** — the ruling is the corrective route the master did not name. `Boundary widening` is still checked first. First occurrence: `conductor-run/tests/journal_conformance.rs`'s unguarded `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` join (security-plan `:115`/`:221`/`:325`), recorded 2026-09-06 as a bounded residual, never routed, closed through `tests/capture_paths` beside the two routed capture readers.

title: D-arch-resources proposes registering an EXTERNAL (non-`CONDUCTOR_*`) environment handle
body:
- pattern: D-arch-resources proposes registering an EXTERNAL (non-`CONDUCTOR_*`) environment handle — one Conductor neither SETS nor READS — into arch §Occupied Resources — Environment variables, where a SHIPPED Conductor artifact (a harness shell's own output, a binary, a committed contract) NAMES it
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — but ONLY on the shipped-artifact clause, which is the whole discriminator. A handle a shipped artifact prints is one a reader will meet and grep for, so leaving it unregistered is a real gap; a handle named only in a chunk report, a plan, a research note or a conversation is NOT registered, because that would make every external knob a document mentions an arch resource. The entry states the three facts that keep the class honest: that Conductor neither sets nor reads it, WHICH shipped artifact names it, and whether it is a run-contract term or a `conductor preconditions` subject (a handle that IS either belongs to those registries instead). Minted 2026-09-07 at the halo-hue-budget-re-driven wrap: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` reached the `run --live` banner in both shells while arch's env registry carried only handles Conductor reads. Escalated because no rule matched and the unease was precedent-shaped — the operator approved the pair and directed this bounding rule so the next wrap cannot over-register.

title: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` handle that is FLAG-valued rather than path-valued (affirmative `"tru
body:
- pattern: a chunk lands a NEW dev-harness-only `CONDUCTOR_*` handle that is FLAG-valued rather than path-valued (affirmative `"true"`/`"1"`, mirroring `conductor_core::flag_declared`), read by `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/wdio.conf.ts` AND by the harness shells, never by a shipped binary, whose effect is to INVERT an existing guard's unresolved-handle outcome (a documented skip-at-exit-0 becomes a non-zero exit) without altering the guard itself — and D-security-input / D-arch-resources propose the security-plan §Input Validation row, the arch env-var registry entry, and the widening of every namespace-wide "the three handles" clause
  verdict: routine
  note: apply as a FOURTH handle class, distinct from all three shipped shapes, and widen every NAMESPACE-WIDE enumeration to the set of four — but NOT the PATH-handle clauses (security-plan's Bootstrap `input-validation-library-install` and the Anti-Patterns canonicalize ban both enumerate PATH handles, and a flag handle is outside their subject; widening them would assert a duty this class does not carry).
